rationale: C22 is a direct drafting template for the child. Both proclamations quote the same portions of sections 9 and 1(e) of title 17, recite a foreign jurisdiction's reciprocal copyright protection, declare fulfillment of the same statutory conditions, confer all title 17 benefits subject to the same section 9(b) exception, and use two matching provisos concerning U.S. formalities and mechanical reproduction rights. The child principally substitutes Monaco and its Sovereign Ordinance for Israel and the official assurances, while adapting the effective dates. C19 is an earlier version of substantially the same template but contains additional Philippines-specific legal recitals. C18 concerns copyright but employs the materially different wartime extension-of-time machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of title 17 of the United States Code, entitled "Copyrights" ... provides in part that the copyright secured by said title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen or subject of a foreign state or nation only
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 9 of title 17 of the United States Code, entitled, "Copyrights" ... provides in part that the copyright secured by such title shall extend to the work of an author or proprietor who is a citizen or subject of a foreign state or nation only
shared_material.explanation: The proclamations open with nearly identical statutory framing and then reproduce the same subsections 9(a) and 9(b).

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of the said title 17 provides in part as follows: "Any person entitled thereto ... (e) to perform the copyrighted work publicly for profit if it be a musical composition"
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 1 of the said title 17 provides in part as follows: "Any person entitled thereto ... (e) To perform the copyrighted work publicly for profit if it be a musical composition"
shared_material.explanation: Both reproduce the same extended section 1(e) passage, including the limitation concerning mechanical reproduction of musical works.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the conditions specified in section (b) and 1(e) of title 17 ... exist and are fulfilled with respect to nationals of the Principality of Monaco ... entitled to all the benefits ... except those ... regarding the extension of time for fulfilling copyright conditions and formalities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the conditions specified in sections 9(b) and 1(e) ... have existed and have been fulfilled with respect to citizens of Israel ... entitled to all the benefits ... except those ... regarding the extension of time for fulfilling copyright conditions and formalities
shared_material.explanation: This is the same operative declaration, with the jurisdiction, temporal formulation, and citizen/national terminology adapted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Provided, that the enjoyment by any work of the rights and benefits conferred by the said title 17 shall be conditioned upon compliance with the requirements and formalities prescribed ... by the copyright laws of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Provided, that the enjoyment by any work of the rights and benefits conferred by the said title 17 shall be conditioned upon compliance with the requirements and formalities prescribed ... by the copyright laws of the United States
shared_material.explanation: The first proviso is essentially verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: And provided further, that the provision of section 1(e) ... shall apply only to compositions published on or after this day, and registered for copyright in the United States which have not been reproduced within the United States prior to this day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: And provided further, that the provisions of section 1(e) ... shall apply only to compositions published after July 1, 1909, and registered for copyright in the United States which have not been reproduced within the United States prior to May 15, 1948
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the parent’s distinctive second-proviso machinery while updating the applicable publication and prior-reproduction dates.
